clue.text: Suggestion: support balls also

parts.note: a prop is something that holds a structure up

indicators.note: to balls something up is to make a mess of it, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offers an idea about holding up some balls as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' looks like a noun being supported, but it is the verb, as in 'balls up', telling you to scramble the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for consideration, a plain synonym for an idea offered.

clue.text: Blair? No, not right to transform Britain

indicators.note: transforming something changes its shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
saying a letter is not there tells you to take it out of the fodder

parts.note: the politician's surname and the word that follows, taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A rejection of Tony Blair's mission to change the country, since he is not right-wing enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the R from BLAIRNO and rearrange BLAINO to get ALBION. 'Not right' reads as a political judgement but simply drops one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Albion is an ancient, poetic name for Britain, still used in literature and football club names.

clue.text: Channel One due to collapse in two minutes

indicators.note: one group of letters sits inside another
something that collapses falls into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
M is the abbreviation for minute, and two of them give a pair
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A TV station, Channel One, is expected to go off the air very soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel One' reads as a TV station name, but 'Channel' is the definition and 'One' is I. The jumbled IDUE goes between two Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist medium acts as a channel between the living and the dead; a medium is also any means of communication.

clue.text: see 24dn.
Constitutional way to mug someone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to roll someone is slang for robbing them

explanation.surface: A lawful, by-the-book method for robbing a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' looks like an adjective meaning legal, but it is the noun: a walk taken for one's health.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is an old-fashioned word for a short walk taken for exercise and health, which is a leisurely amble.

clue.text: Backsliding Dotty Rees grabs genital area

indicators.note: something that grabs holds another thing within its grip
dotty means crazy or scatty, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the name taken as written before being rearranged
the lap is the front of the body from waist to knees when seated

explanation.surface: A woman called Dotty Rees, having lapsed morally, makes a grope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like a first name for Rees, but it is the anagram signal. The lap, where one sits, is a coy euphemism for the genital area.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into a former bad state or habit, which is what backsliding describes.

clue.text: Get physical when criminal Ray opens till

indicators.note: to open something up is to break into its middle, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to till soil is to plough it

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: the name taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook named Ray breaks open the cash register, and things turn violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' is a cash register in the surface but the farming verb in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To play rough is to use force or violence, an idiom for turning aggressive, just as getting physical does.

clue.text: Orange order pact with Rio

indicators.note: putting things in a new order means rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Orange Order, a Protestant fraternity in Northern Ireland, makes a deal with Rio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange order' reads as the Northern Irish Protestant Orange Order; split them, and 'Orange' is the definition while 'order' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricot is a pale yellowish-orange colour, named after the fruit, so it is a shade of orange.

clue.text: Bastard northern mobster's side

parts.note: an arse is British slang for a contemptible person, like a bastard
N is the abbreviation for northern
Al Capone is the archetypal mobster, so AL stands for him

explanation.surface: A nasty northern gangster's team or faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is the definition, a sports team. Arse is British slang for a fool or nasty person; Al Capone supplies the mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous London football club, and a side is a team in British sporting usage.

clue.text: Song about leaving Cyclops with a mess

indicators.note: making a mess of things throws them into disorder
when something leaves it is no longer present, so it is taken away

parts.note: C is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about
the setter's name, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A song about the setter Cyclops walking out and leaving chaos behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it is C (circa), removed from CYCLOPS; add A and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a style of Caribbean folk music from Trinidad, so a calypso is a kind of song.

clue.text: Rather formal group of stars will present future test for Trump

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and formal
Aries is a constellation, the Ram

explanation.surface: A stuffy constellation will put on a forthcoming exam for Donald Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of stars' suggests celebrities but means a constellation. In the US, presidential candidates must first win their party's primary elections.
explanation.definitionFit: Primaries are the preliminary US elections in which a party picks its presidential candidate, a hurdle Trump faced.

clue.text: Burst of criticism: "Short girl, five nothing"

indicators.note: making a word short means cutting letters from its end

parts.note: Sally is a girl's name
V is the Roman numeral for five
the letter O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A cutting remark about a small girl being scored five out of nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten SALLY to SAL (itself a short form of the name), then add V and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is literally a simultaneous discharge of guns, and figuratively a sudden attack of words or complaints.

clue.text: The Sun almost managed to turn round a batty feature

indicators.note: almost all of something means the last bit is missing

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the Sun

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper nearly succeeded in rescuing a crazy publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sun' looks like the British tabloid, but it is SOL cut to SO. 'Batty' means crazy in the surface and 'of bats' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats navigate by echolocation, a natural form of sonar, so sonar is a feature of bats.

clue.text: City-related, pathetic Ukip claim: "Nigel's head for a thousand!"

indicators.note: something pathetic is feeble and in a sorry state, so the letters fall apart
one thing given for another means it replaces it

parts.note: taken as written before changes

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the name
K is the abbreviation for a thousand

explanation.surface: A feeble boast from UKIP, the Eurosceptic party then led by Nigel Farage, offering a grand for his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the K in UKIPCLAIM for N, then rearrange. The quoted 'claim' looks like a bounty, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal describes things belonging to a town or city's local government, so it is an adjective for city matters.

clue.text: Corner Conservative veteran and become snotty-nosed?

parts.note: to corner someone is to catch them
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a veteran is old

explanation.surface: Trap an old Tory and turn haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snotty-nosed' in the surface means stuck-up; the question mark flags its literal sense of a runny nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching a cold leaves you with a runny nose, so the phrase describes getting a literal snotty nose.

clue.text: Opposition party's going round story-telling? Must be good for a successful business

definitions.note: the clue is a description of the answer rather than a synonym

relation is the act of relating, or telling, a story

explanation.surface: The opposition party goes around spinning yarns, which must be fine for a booming firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Labour Party was then the main opposition in the UK parliament. The possessive 'S' wraps round RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour relations are dealings between management and workers, and harmony there helps any company thrive.

clue.text: Stomach three-quarters oversize? This'll flatten it!

definitions.note: a cryptic description referring back to the stomach

indicators.note: keeping three parts of four means one letter is cut off

parts.note: to stomach something is to tolerate or bear it
huge means extremely large

explanation.surface: A big belly mostly too large? A tight squeeze will press it flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like the noun, the belly, but in the wordplay it is the verb meaning tolerate. HUGE loses its last quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear hug is a tight, crushing embrace, the sort that would squash a protruding belly.

clue.text: House high point of crap, or of pot

indicators.note: something crap is rubbish and badly put together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: The crowning glory of a house is either poo or pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crap' reads as part of the subject matter, but it is the signal to rearrange the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooftop is the uppermost outer surface of a building, the topmost part of a house.

clue.text: Pissed off with mugging

definitions.meaning: first meaning: furious, in a rage
second meaning: British slang for a gang robbing a crowd by rushing through it

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 'steaming' was 1980s slang for gangs charging through a train carriage or crowd and robbing passengers; it is also slang for very angry, or very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming describes someone seething with anger, and it also names a type of gang robbery by a rushing crowd.

clue.text: Group tossed yobs east side of ground

indicators.note: in an across answer east is the right, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: a beach is a stretch of sandy ground by the sea

indicators.note: things tossed are thrown about and land in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A gang of thugs gets thrown out of the east stand at a football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' looks like a gang but is a band. Yobs are British louts; scrambled they become BOYS, placed to the right of BEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beach Boys are a famous American pop band from California, and a group is a band of musicians.

clue.text: Wanting beer brewed, a small measure

indicators.note: brewing mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
FT is the abbreviation for foot, a small unit of length

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like desiring, but it means lacking; 'a small measure' suggests a tot of drink but is a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means deprived or lacking something, which matches wanting in its sense of being without.

explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, so they are abbreviated SE for South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Hack is a disparaging word for a journalist or jobbing writer, and scribe is a jocular term for the same.

clue.text: Pure cocaine given up for speed

clue.text: Undergarment … shudder!

clue.text: Wicked females ousting leader, which doesn't bode well
